We've covered several reports about Apple Vision Pro applications in medical settings. This week, Stryker announced the completion of the first surgical procedure using an innovative application on Vision Pro.

The procedure was a hip arthroscopy, using an application called SportSuite Vision, which brings 'critical digital content into the surgeon's virtual space,' including arthroscopic imaging, HipCheck, HipMap, and CT scan images.

Here's Stryker's introduction to the application:

SportSuite Vision brings critical digital content into the surgeon's visual space, allowing them to simultaneously see physical objects and digital tools such as arthroscopic imaging, HipCheck, HipMap, and CT scan images in the operating room. During arthroscopic procedures, surgeons often need to rely on multiple displays placed throughout the operating room to access imaging and surgical data. By consolidating multiple data sources into the doctor's field of view, this technology can reduce reliance on traditional monitors and support a more streamlined, ergonomic surgical workflow.

SportSuite Vision received FDA De Novo authorization on July 17. Stryker stated this is the first application approved by the FDA for use with Vision Pro during surgery.
